queries.text: Schopenhauer, “The Metaphysics of Love of the Sexes,” translated from the author’s Portuguese; the public-domain English version is R. B. Haldane and J. Kemp’s (The World as Will and Idea, vol. III).
Lévi, translated from the author’s Portuguese; compare Waite’s public-domain “Transcendental Magic.” “LËVI” in the original corrected to LÉVI. “Mago”/“bruxo” rendered “magus”/“sorcerer.”
Matthew 5:41, translated from the author’s Portuguese (“légua” = league; “inimigo” = enemy). The King James Version reads: “And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain.”
